content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigates the few-shot temporal action localization where only a few support videos with novel classes are available during evaluation. To solve this problem, the authors use prompt training based on CLIP.  The class-wise token embedding is learned from annotated videos and is then combined with the text features.  Experiments are conducted on two benchmark datasets including THUMOS14 and ActivityNet datasets. The proposed method archives highest performance among all compared methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The paper investigates a practical problem while the few-shot action localization is introduced.
2. The method uses the CLIP model with prompt tunning, which is quite interesting in the action localization setting. 
3. The proposed method shows great improvement from the experimental results. 


Weakness
1. The method part is a bit hard to follow. In page 4, the support feature $E_{s} \in R^{N\times K \times D \times L}$ while the support feature in page 5 is $E_{s} \in R^{K \times D \times L}$. There are six losses in the training, but only two objectives are shown in the paper. 
2. The paper introduces the prompt multimodal learning for few-shot action localization. However, how the proposed method outperforms other methods(no-prompt, no learnable prompt) is not well studied.  Some visualization results should be provided for comparisons.
3. Comparisons are not sufficient. Why only 5-shot is compared in Table 1?  
4. This paper studies the action localization problem while action detection is called in the paper.  Action detection usually denotes spatial-temporal action detection.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The main method in the proposed few-shot action localization setting is new, but the main contribution of the method is not well-written and is a bit hard to follow.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, this paper introduces a few-shot action localization problem and uses the CLIP-based model to extract video features for learning adaptive representations. The method is new in this area but the writing needs to be improved. Moreover, the experimental results do not sufficiently demonstrate why the proposed method localizes the action in videos. Therefore, I tend to reject the current version.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work introduce a new TAD task combing both few-shot and zero-shot TAD tasks. Meanwhile, a Multi-Modality Prompt Meta-Learning framework is proposed and achieve great experiment results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
* Introduce a new TAD task, which combines the setting of Few-shot and Zero-shot TAD tasks. This combination is not meaningless, since we usually known the class name of support videoes. 
* Propose an effective framework to utilize both visual and textual context with prompt learning.
* Great experiment results are achieved in both ActivityNet and THUMOS dataset.

Weekness：
* Authors should give simple description of N-way K-shot experiment for readers not familar with meta learning.
* For 1-way setting, is it same as temporal action proposal generation task? As the proposed method mainly focus on classifier, can authors give more discussion about how multi-modal framework help the action localizer?
* The description of multi-modal few-shot learning baseline methods are not clear. For example, how authors modify PromptDet to suit MMFS definition? What means adapted CoCOOP to STABLE? For readers not familar with these baseline methods, this part is very confusing. Authors should at least describe the setting of these baseline methods in supplementary.
* The ablation study of proposed method is not sufficient. By directly removing the support videos part (degraded to Zero-shot setting) or textual part (degraded to Few-shot setting) of proposed model,  we can get proper ablation baselines to prove the effectiveness of proposed multi-modal framework.
* For visual transformer, is it trained with rest modules end-to-end?
* A minor suggestion, authors can enlarge the font size  in Fig 3.
content.summary_of_the_review: In conclusion, this work propose a valuable new TAD task along with a reasonable new method. My concern is mainly about the experiment parts, where the comparison with MMFS baselines are not clear enough.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work tackles the problem of conventional temporal action detection (TAD) and focuses on a novel multimodal setting. They achieve this by mapping few-shot support videos to the textual token space of a pretrained ViL model. Experimental evaluations on  two benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed model achieves the State-of-the-art performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength**  

1.  This paper is well-organized and easy to follow.  
2. The authors conducted extensive experiments including both comparison to the SOTA and several ablation studies, the proposed method outperforms all the baselines and the ablation studies verify the effective model design.

**Weakness**

1. Writing. 
  - There are a lot of typos in the paper and the whole texts need to be carefully revised. 
  - The method section is not well-demonstrated. E.g. equation 1~7 are not necessarily highlighted, all of them just illustrate some functional modules; In the first paragraph of section 3, the problem setting of the MMFE-TAD is unclear. There is no clear definition of \mathcal{C} (similarly, no definition of \mathbb{Q} and \mathbb{V} in eq 7) and also what's the key difference of MMFE-TAD and a normal TAD in term of the problem setting?

2. Novelty: The proposed method is based on all previous architectures, (CLIP and visual / text transformer), and objectives (tok loss). It's a little bit hard to tell the great performance is from all the previous powerlful modules or the actual model design.

**Some other questions**

1. Experimental evaluations 
- For table 1, for the MMFS competers, as the author claimed, the MMFS is a novel problem setting and there is no exsiting baselines. The authors mentioned "We replaced their backbones with pre-trained frozen CLIP ViT encoders and the object decoders with TAD decoders". Does that mean the baselines use a fixed CLIP-ViT to extract visual-language features, instead of their own (visual) feature extractors? 
- Furthermore, also for table 1, PromptDet and OWL-ViT are used for MMFS setting but meta-DeTR and Feat-RW are used for the FS setting. In Sec. 4 setting the authors mentioned all the object-detection models are adapted with a CLIP-ViT encoder, then why the two methods cannot work for MMFS setting?
- For Table 1, why the MUPPET in the last line did not take the text feature as the other MUPPET models? Is that a typo? 
- Finally, still for Table 1, if for all the comparison baselines, the feature extracting backbones, and the decoders are changed from the original implementation, also the encoders are fixed, even if the proposed method can outperform all of the models, how to verify these results are convincing? 
- Combining Table 2 and Table 1, we could see the LTP model performs worse than EffDet, STALE and baseline 1, and all of them only takes the text features. However, due to lacking of details of the baselines, it's hard to see if that's a fair comparison.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
See the previous section for questions and detailed comments.

For the quality, the model is well-designed and the experimental comparison is sufficient. The paper organization and formulation could be further improved. The novelty might be an issue but I would like to further consider it based on the author's response.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the current version of the paper is not good enough for ICLR though personally I think the problem and model architecture is interesting. I currently give a reject since I don't think the current version of the paper is good enough. But I will re-consider the rating after hearing from the authors and considering the opinions from other reviewers.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to tackle the problem setting of temporal action detection with multimodal prompts: textual description and exemplar videos. Visual features are extracted using CLIP-model-based frame features and additional self-attention modules. Multi-modal prompt is constructed to combine the visual and target text embedding. Finally, actions are classified and localized. Experiments on two datasets show the efficacy of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The proposed method achieves significantly better than previous methods.

Weaknesses
1. The proposed multimodal few-shot temporal action detection task is not really a new task. Previously a series of TRECVID Multimedia Event Detection tasks hosted by NIST [1*, 2*] already presented competitors with “event kits” for video classification: a few exemplar videos and textual descriptions of the event/action. Please provide the connection between the proposed task and the aforementioned one in the related work discussion for better reference.
2. The method part is a bit confusing to me. 
(1) What is the relation between the episodic video features F_{T_i} (Eqn. 1) and episodic adapter features F_E? Does L << t, which means variable length videos are sub-sampled into a fixed number (L) of features? 
(2) Before Eqn.9, it says “given t-th snippet” (of length L?), and then later “i-th snippet” is used to describe [1, L], which is also very confusing.
(3) L is used to represent model outputs (Eqn. 5 & 6) and also losses (Eqn.10 & 11).
(4) “ Grounded on the pretrained (frozen) ViL model”. “Our model is trained end-to-end in each stage, with the pretrained text encoder frozen.” So do the authors train the visual encoder of CLIP?
(5) For experiments with Kinetics-400 pretraining, do the authors still use CLIP text encoder? (since K400 is an action classification dataset and there is no accompanying caption)

[1*] Awad, George, et al. "Trecvid 2016: Evaluating video search, video event detection, localization, and hyperlinking." TREC Video Retrieval Evaluation (TRECVID). 2016.
[2*] Liang, J., Chen, J., Huang, P., Li, X., Jiang, L., Lan, Z., ... & Hauptmann, A. G. (2016). Informedia@ TRECVID 2016. In TRECVID.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The method part needs a lot more work to make it clearer. The proposed task is somewhat novel but lacks an explanation of when such a  task is applicable in real-world scenarios. The method part is too convoluted for me so I don’t think the results can be easily reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: I’m leaning towards rejection mainly due to the method part. Much clarification is needed.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
